author: Y.Imaizumi <40021161+vorj@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Improve IndexPQFastScan and IndexIVFPQFastScan performance for aarch64 devices (#1815)

Summary:
related: https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/issues/1812

This PR improves the performance of `IndexPQFastScan` and `IndexIVFPQFastScan` on aarch64 devices, e.g., 60x faster on an AWS Arm instance with the SIFT1M dataset.
The contents of this PR are below:

- Add `simdlib_neon.h`
    - `simdlib_neon.h` has `simdlib` compatible API, and they are implemented with Arm NEON intrinsics.
    - `simdlib.h` includes `simdlib_neon.h` if `__aarch64__` is defined.
- Move `geteven` , `getodd` , `getlow128` , and `gethigh128` from `distances_simd.cpp` to `simdlib_avx2.h` .
- Port `geteven` , `getodd` , `getlow128` , and `gethigh128` for non-AVX2 environments.
    - These codes are implemented with AVX2 intrinsics, so they have prevented to implement `compute_PQ_dis_tables_dsub2` for non-AVX2 environments.
    - Now `simdlib_avx2.h` , `simdlib_emulated.h` , and `simdlib_neon.h` all have those functions.
- Enable `compute_PQ_dis_tables_dsub2` on aarch64
    - Above change makes `compute_PQ_dis_tables_dsub2` independent from `geteven` and so on.
    - `compute_PQ_dis_tables_dsub2` implemented with `simdlib_neon.h` is little faster than current implementation, so enabling that.
        - In contrast, `compute_PQ_dis_tables_dsub2` implemented with `simdlib_emulated.h` is slower than current implementation, so we have not enabled it in our PR.

author: Stuart Prescott <stuart@debian.org>
commit message:
Fix tests to find resources without changing dir

Test resources are in the same directory (or a child directory) of the test
code so the code can locate the resources itself rather than relying on the
tests being run from a certain location. This allows the tests to be used to
test the installed code rather than the current checkout and also allows
automated test discovery with tools like py.test to be used, running all
tests at once without a runner.

author: Ryan Murphy <ryan.murphy@nist.gov>
commit message:
Adding Irena results for usaxs alumina data

SizeDistribution fit results from Irena. Note: A power-law function is subtracted from the alumina I(q) data. B = 9.64827e-5, P = 3.27172, Bkg = 0.120605. B is the power-law scaling factor fit at low-q. P is the power-law slope fit at low-q. Bkg is the flat background at high-q. From what I can understand, the fit is being performed on the subtracted I(q) data. For example, I_sub(q) = I_data(q) - I_power(q), where I_power(q) = B*q^(-P) + Bkg. This is equivalent to the "power_law" model located in sasmodels.

If the data is slit-smeared, we would need to subtract instead a slit-smeared form of the power_law model from the data.

commit message:
Fix Sv calculation, error and display

The Sv was being calculated in a circular manner and provided completely
bogus uncertainty.  Sv is fundamentally based on the porod constant and
contrast with are both user inputs with NO uncertainty estimate (would
be nice to get some?).  Redid the computation to use those values
directly so that it will display even if vol fraction has an error.
Also replaced error with NONE if ds ==0. I actually included code do
properly compute the uncertainty if uncertainties are ever given on
Porod Constant and contrast..

Also replace NaN with ERROR  both for s and phi and added a logger
statement that goes to the log file but currently NOTHING is going to
the console screen as mentioned in another ticket somewhere.

Updated AnnulusSlicer to improve slicer min limits (low-q 2D data) and max limits (offset 2D data)

commit message:
Stop using __file__ to find resources

Using __file__ to find resources is hopelessly complicated across the different
frozen modules, debug modules, unpacked source etc that are used to run sasview.
importlib.resource provides a uniform interface to finding resources that are
shipped alongside modules.

Since the `config_file` member is not used anywhere outside this class,
let's also make it 'private' since it's a file-like object that should
be private to the module.

commit message:
Improve efficiency of CanSAS 2.0 reader

When it came to reading the Q and I data values, the reader was looping
through every single data point in the hdf5 file and appending it to an
array. This caused problems when loading very large files, rendering
SasView unresponsive. Now, the reader saves the entire array from the
file, instead of looping through each point.

author: Paul Butler <butlerpd@udel.edu>
commit message:
Fix vol fraction uncertainty calculation

The vol frac uncertainty calculation uses dy of course. but if the data
had not dy, the code decided to create a dy=sqrt(y).  This is only valid
for raw counts not reduced data. Creating a completely bogus uncertainty
in order to then propagate is just wrong.  Changed so that if the data
has no uncertainty the vol frac uncertainty is given as -1

Actually the value is bogus anyway since the real uncertainty depends on
how much of the curve is being captured correctly but that we can't do
much about.

author: rjbourne <57537928+rjbourne@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
adjusts the error system for loading files

This adds two main changes:
 - the use of logger was switched to logging to ensure that the message also displays on the log screen of the GUI - otherwise the user could load a file with errors in, and the user would not be informed of the fact that lines of the file may have been altered
 - An error loading the file which previously raised an exception now gives an error on the logger and cancels the file load. This resolves the previous issue that bad files would not display an error to the user, but simply appear to continue loading forever.

through every single data point in the hdf5 file and appending it to an
array. This caused problems when loading very large files, rendering
SasView unresponsive. Now, the reader saves the entire array from the
file, instead of looping through each point.

author: Ryan Murphy <ryan.murphy@nist.gov>
commit message:
Adding Irena results for usaxs alumina data

SizeDistribution fit results from Irena. Note: A power-law function is subtracted from the alumina I(q) data. B = 9.64827e-5, P = 3.27172, Bkg = 0.120605. B is the power-law scaling factor fit at low-q. P is the power-law slope fit at low-q. Bkg is the flat background at high-q. From what I can understand, the fit is being performed on the subtracted I(q) data. For example, I_sub(q) = I_data(q) - I_power(q), where I_power(q) = B*q^(-P) + Bkg. This is equivalent to the "power_law" model located in sasmodels.

If the data is slit-smeared, we would need to subtract instead a slit-smeared form of the power_law model from the data.

commit message:
Clean up the width nomenclature and simplify width calc code.

The review comments asked for the dictionary set params for x and y widths be standardized. In fact it turned out that a) the widths were actually half widths and b) there was a variety of words used. The entire BoxSlicer.py code now uses half_width and half_height (and half_width_min etc).

Also as per review, the abs(half_width/height) from set params was removed. It turns out the values should never be negative but it is unclear whether absoluting them if they end up negative (which should not be possible at this point)  will yield the correct answer. Thus better for it to fail.

also corrected the nbins calculation in _post_data for direction="Y" (the plus should have been a minus)

commit message:
Improve efficiency of CanSAS 2.0 reader

When it came to reading the Q and I data values, the reader was looping
through every single data point in the hdf5 file and appending it to an
array. This caused problems when loading very large files, rendering
SasView unresponsive. Now, the reader saves the entire array from the
file, instead of looping through each point.

Merge master

see issue #590. fix error in q.rg and uncertainties in Rg and I0.
Uncertainty calculation for slope and intercept are still wrong I
believe.

references #205 - Removed Kratky plot choice from linearized plots for
now since it doesn't currently work.

close #590.  A lot of problems were caused by LineModel and LinerFit
having different equations (ax+b vs a+bx).  Further errors in
calculations, particularly of uncertainties were fixed. The fact that
the fits to not account for smearing was verified and a warning added.
Code was also modified to update the qmin and qmax to match changes in
the transformed xmin xmax.  Lots of documentation was added and the
fitdialog layout was cleaned up considerably.  This is now usable though
the design of the user interface (and the whole design of linear fits)
could use a rethink.

Fix compatibility with matplotlib 3.5.x

This patch attempts to fix compatibility with matplotlib 3.5.x by updating
the code to avoid functions that were deprecated (in some cases for years)
and have now been removed.

Merging this patch at least allows the sasview GUI to start with matplotlib
3.5; additional places where code needs to be updated may well be uncovered
by automated or manual testing.

Closes: #2170

commit message:
improvement of edge cases in fourier transform

The previous version of this algorithm simply added a small epsilon value to each Q to ensure the vectors did not line up with the element faces - which would cause divide by zero errors - instead special case algorithms have been implemented so epsilon is only used where necessary - and L'Hospital is used where possible.

This is the first working case of this algorithm and several improvements have yet to be added, such as direction specific epsilon vectors, and exploring the range for which L'Hospital's limit can be used.

author: Paul Butler <butlerpd@udel.edu>
commit message:
Fix Pr failure ticket #273
 
 Long version:  In August 2013 it was determined that many instability problems experienced by SasView were do to a threading problem in fitting.py.  Mainly the authors seemed to not realize that calling thread.stop just raised a flag and that the thread itself needed to check for said flag regularly and kill the thread if it found the flag raised.  A quick fix was implemented by adding a wait till the existing thread ended naturally to the two places in the code where the stop is raised.  This seems to work.  

At the same time pr.py was found to use the same raising of the stop flag three times and it was assumed that the same problem existed and the same wait “fix” was implemented.  Subsequenty it has been shown that the new wait code in pr.py NEVER gets reached and thus the fix breaks the PrView perspective.  It may be that this earlier code properly dealt with threads properly(still remembering how the thread code was meant to be used).  Whatever the case will remove this fix for now.   

Finally another thread.stop was found once in simulation.py.  since this is older code it may also be handled properly so am removing the “Fix” from that as well for now.

to quickly find these points in the future: 
fitting.py - two instances that seem to need fixing
pr.py - three instances that may work correctly
simulation.py - one instace

search terms:
“-PDB” or
“d.stop” (thread.stop or thread_1D.stop or 2D.stop)

Make `Adduct` a subclass of `Geometry`
`Adduct` can be considered a special case of `Geometry`, with additional methods/attributes available. It is not stored in the `geometry` module, however, to break modules into more manageable size. This decision considers that a given workflow may or may not utilize `Adduct`, but `Geometry` will be used in all cases.
